newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Telekom sets issue price at 28.50 dmk.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Telekom sets issue price at 28.50 dmk.

text.p: German telecommunications firm Deutsche Telekom AG said on Sunday its first-ever placement of shares, the biggest flotation ever in Europe and the second largest in the world, was oversubscribed by five times .

At a news conference in Frankfurt, Telekom chief executive Ron Sommer said private and institutional investors would be allotted shares at a price of 28.50 marks ($18.92) each, a slightly lower price than the 30 mark ticket markets had been expecting.
The total issue of 713 million shares would raise about 20 billion marks, making it uncontestably Europe's largest-ever initial public offering, Sommer said.
"With this volume of proceeds, our flotation is Europe's biggest ever and the second biggest in the world," Sommer said.
Of the total issue volume, 33 percent had gone to investors outside Germany, where interest had been very strong, he said.
"Foreign investors took up around 33 percent of the floated shares. The demand was many times this and represented a volume of more than 30 billion marks," he said.
In the United States, the company's American Depository Shares will be issued at $18.89 each, chief financial officer Joachim Kroeske said.

Although more than 50 percent was likely to be taken up by institutional investors, Sommer noted that Telekom had been unusually successful in drumming up interest from private German investors, who traditionally fight shy of investment in the "risky" stock market.
These small shareholders, who have been wooed by Telekom in blanket advertising campaign, would be guaranteed a minimum of 100 shares each and would take up 315 million shares in total, he said.
Telekom shares, which will immediately take a dominant role in Germany's 30-share DAX stock market index, will begin trading on stock markets around the globe from November 18.
Nicole Cousins, telecoms analyst at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt, said she believed the lower-than-expected price for the issue meant there was a good chance of price gains once trading began.

"28.50 is below our expectations, we thought it would come in at the high end of the range (30 marks)" she said. "Based on our benchmarks we thought it was fairly valued at 30 marks. There is room for price appreciation based on fundamentals."
Telekom AG said it would use the 20 billion marks or so raised in its the placement to strengthen its balance sheet by paying off outstanding debt.
The company's chief financial officer Joachim Kroeske told a news conference that the proceeds would be used "completely" to settle debts. ($1=1.5063 Mark)
